sentences.text:
Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025
 High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravati

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Main Case No. W.P.No.35421 of 2025
 Proceeding Sheet
Sl. Date Order Office
No. Note
 19.12.2025 Vn, J

This writ petition is filed declaring the action
 of Respondents in not considering the case of
the Petitioner for appointment and not allowing the Petitioner to un
dergo for training for the Post of Police Constable on the ground of pendency of criminal case as illegal and arbitrary
. A notification was issued on 28.11.2022 for recruitment of Police Constables by Respondent No.2.

The Petitioner,
being eligible, applied and was selected for the post of Police Constable.
However, he was not being sent for training on the premise that a criminal case is pending.
Hence, the present writ petition.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that a case in FIR.No.229 of 2021 dated 15.12.2021 under Sections 376(2)(N), 354-D(1), 354-C and 417 IPC has been registered against the Petitioner and his family members in connection with dispute between his elder brother and the complainant and in that context, Petitioner was arrayed as A.3 though no specific attributions were made in the charge sheet against the Petitioner.
subsequently, both complainant and brother of the Petitioner get married with others separately.
Therefore, mere pendency of the criminal case cannot come in the way of Petitioner being sent for training for being appointed as Police Constable.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader Sri S.Raju on instructions submits that it would be impermissible to appoint a person as a Police Constable even though he is facing a criminal case.

In the present case, the nature of the criminal case against the Petitioner is with regard to the offences under Sections 376(2)(N),
354-D(1), 354-C and 417 IPC, and it is not advisable to send such persons for training.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties.

It is to be noted that criminal case cannot be an absolute bar for sending an individual selected for training and the Respondent- authorities are required to examine the nature of allegations against the Petitioner in the charge sheet and then take a conscious decision whether to send the person to training as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Avtar Singh v. Union of India and others (2016 Supreme (SC) 578).

entities.text: Avtar Singh v. Union of India and others (2016 Supreme (SC) 578)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of the order is extracted below:
30........

(5) In a case where the employee has made declaration truthfully of a concluded criminal case, the employer still has the right to consider antecedents, and cannot be compelled to appoint the candidate.

(6) In case when fact has been truthfully declared in character verification form regarding pendency of a criminal case of trivial nature, employer, in facts and circumstances of the Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28155267/
1 case, in its discretion may appoint the candidate subject to decision of such case.

Hence, there shall be interim direction to the Respondents as under:
(i) The Petitioner shall submit a representation along with authentic copy of the charge sheet to the Respondents within a period of two weeks.
(ii) The Respondents shall thereupon examine the charge sheet and the allegations against the Petitioner and shall pass appropriate orders on the representation within a further period of two weeks.
Post after six weeks.
